findings.body:
**Prevent `.gitattributes` from hiding scanned content.**

At `.github/workflows/denylist.yml`, Line 102, a PR can add `credentials.txt -diff` to `.gitattributes` and put a prohibited value in `credentials.txt`. Git then emits a binary-file summary instead of its text diff. Gitleaks v8.30.1 skips non-archive binary diffs, so the check can pass. The octopus scan has the same exposure. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes))

Add `--text` to both `--log-opts` values, or otherwise prevent untrusted attributes from suppressing text diffs. Git documents `--text` as treating all files as text. Make the correction in the template and regenerate this workflow. As per path instructions, “Workflow edits route through policy/templates/ re-instantiation, never direct edits.” ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log))
findings.title: Prevent `.gitattributes` from hiding scanned content.

findings.body:
**Remove scanned-revision `.gitleaksignore` overrides.**

At `.github/workflows/denylist.yml`, Line 102, `--config` does not disable `.gitleaksignore`. Gitleaks v8.30.1 also loads that file from the scanned source. A PR can add a prohibited value and its `file:rule-id:start-line` fingerprint, then pass the check without changing the trusted TOML. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))

Remove the scanned revision's `.gitleaksignore`, or replace it with a trusted copy before all scans. Setting `--gitleaks-ignore-path` alone is insufficient because v8.30.1 separately loads the source-local file. Apply the correction in `policy/templates/denylist.yml` and re-instantiate this workflow. As per path instructions, “Workflow edits route through policy/templates/ re-instantiation, never direct edits.” ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))
findings.title: Remove scanned-revision `.gitleaksignore` overrides.

findings.body:
**Disable inline allow directives in every scan.**

At `.github/workflows/denylist.yml`, Line 113, a commit message can contain a prohibited value and `gitleaks:allow` on the same line. Gitleaks v8.30.1 discards that finding by default. The same bypass affects both `gitleaks git` calls, independently of `.gitleaksignore`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))

Add `--ignore-gitleaks-allow` to all three scanner calls so PR-controlled content cannot override the trusted policy. Make the change in the template and re-instantiate the workflow. As per path instructions, “Workflow edits route through policy/templates/ re-instantiation, never direct edits.” ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8.30.1/cmd/root.go))
findings.title: Disable inline allow directives in every scan.
